chunks: Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the printed garment, can a man enter into Ihram while wearing it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but what is disliked is the silk-blended (garment).

key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: Enters into the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a man wear printed clothes while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on men's Ihram garments is not against printed or patterned cloth (*thawb mu'allam*), but specifically against silk (*mulhham*). This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on material composition over aesthetic design when determining the validity of Ihram attire, resolving potential confusion between general patterned clothing and the specific prohibition of silk.
